output.summary: The shrink increase is mainly a receiving-control failure, not theft. DSD categories account for 73% of the increase. The receiving clerk was removed in 41 stores in April 2025, and shrink there rose to 3.0% against 1.7% in the 17 clerk stores. Audit counts found 4.9% over-invoicing. A reinstatement pilot with matched controls cut DSD shrink from 4.4% to 1.9%, and the vendor credits recovered far exceeded the labor cost. District 4's associate-theft policy suppressed shortage claims and produced one $14 bag-check recovery. POS exception rates and theft terminations were flat, which argues against associate theft. The count-firm switch is not an artifact. ORC is real but small and unquantified. Locked cases lost more margin than the shrink they saved. Reinstate receiving first. Do not roll out cameras, LP officers or locked cases chain-wide yet.
